title: Modules and imports
summary: Share values and types between modules using explicit imports and exports.
rules: Type-only imports and exports are erased from emitted JavaScript.
Import paths and module resolution depend on the project configuration.
Named imports use exported names; a default import can use a local name.

title: Variables and inference
summary: Declare block-scoped bindings with inferred or explicit types.
rules: const prevents reassignment of the binding; it does not freeze an object.
let and const are block-scoped; var is function-scoped.
Prefer inference where the initializer communicates the type.

title: Primitive and special types
summary: Use primitive types for values and special types for unknown or impossible values.
rules: Use lowercase primitive names rather than boxed String, Number, or Boolean.
unknown requires narrowing before value-specific operations; any bypasses checking.
never represents values that cannot occur; void is used when a return value is not consumed.

title: Functions and parameters
summary: Describe callable behavior with typed parameters and return values.
rules: Optional parameters must follow required parameters.
A rest parameter must be last.
Return types can often be inferred; explicit annotations document public contracts.

title: Arrow functions
summary: Create function expressions, often as callbacks that capture surrounding values.
rules: Parenthesize an object literal returned by an expression body.
Arrow functions capture this from the surrounding scope.
Callback parameter types can be inferred from the receiving API.

title: Object types and properties
summary: Describe object shape with required, optional, and readonly properties.
rules: An optional property may be absent; reading it includes undefined.
readonly prevents assignments through that typed reference and is shallow.
Object compatibility is structural; excess property checks apply to fresh literals.

title: Interfaces and extension
summary: Name an object contract and extend existing contracts.
rules: Interfaces describe structural contracts; they do not create runtime objects.
Compatible interface declarations of the same name can merge.
Use extends to add properties; incompatible inherited properties are errors.

title: Type aliases
summary: Give any type expression a reusable name.
rules: Aliases can name primitives, unions, tuples, functions, and object types.
Aliases are erased and cannot be used as runtime constructors.
Unlike interfaces, aliases cannot be reopened by declaration merging.

title: Unions and intersections
summary: Combine possible alternatives with | and simultaneous requirements with &.
rules: A union permits any member; operations must be safe for every remaining member.
An intersection requires all constituent constraints.
Literal types restrict values to particular strings, numbers, or booleans.

title: Narrowing and type guards
summary: Refine possible types using control flow and checked predicates.
rules: Use null checks before treating an unknown value as an object.
Discriminated unions share a property with distinct literal values.
A user-defined type predicate is a promise to the checker; its implementation must validate that promise.

title: Generic parameters and constraints
summary: Relate input and output types using reusable type parameters.
rules: Type arguments can be inferred from values or supplied explicitly.
A constraint limits allowed type arguments and the operations available in the body.
Generic types are erased at runtime.

title: Arrays and transformations
summary: Describe ordered collections and transform them with array methods.
rules: Array<Type> and Type[] describe the same mutable array type.
map produces a new array; filter retains matching values.
A readonly array prevents mutation through that reference and is shallow.

title: Tuples
summary: Describe positional elements with a known sequence of types.
rules: Tuple positions have specific types and may carry documentation labels.
Optional elements follow required ones.
Readonly tuples prevent assignment through the typed reference.

title: Destructuring and spread
summary: Extract fields and elements, or assemble shallow copies.
rules: Object renaming uses property: local; defaults apply only to undefined.
Spread copies enumerable own object properties or iterates array elements.
Copies are shallow; nested objects remain shared.

title: Loops and iteration
summary: Repeat work over iterables or while a condition holds.
rules: for...of consumes iterable values; for...in enumerates enumerable string keys including inherited keys.
break exits the loop and continue advances to its next iteration.
for await...of belongs in an async function or a module supporting top-level await.

title: Maps and keyed lookup
summary: Store key/value entries in a typed Map.
rules: get returns Value | undefined when a key might be absent.
Keys can be arbitrary values; object keys are compared by identity.
Map iteration follows insertion order.

title: Sets and uniqueness
summary: Store unique values with a typed Set.
rules: Duplicate entries are retained only once.
Object entries are compared by identity.
Iteration follows insertion order.

title: Promises and async functions
summary: Represent asynchronous results with promises and await them inside async functions.
rules: An async function always returns a promise.
await unwraps fulfillment or throws the rejection reason.
Promise.all rejects when any input rejects; allSettled records every outcome.

title: Exceptions and unknown errors
summary: Throw exceptions and handle caught values safely.
rules: JavaScript can throw any value; strict TypeScript treats caught values as unknown.
Narrow the caught value before reading Error properties.
finally runs when leaving try/catch; a return or throw there can replace the earlier outcome.

title: Classes and access modifiers
summary: Define instances with state, methods, inheritance, and access restrictions.
rules: A derived constructor must call super before using this.
TypeScript private/protected are checked statically; #fields provide JavaScript runtime privacy.
implements checks the instance contract without adding members or method parameter types.

title: Optional chaining and nullish defaults
summary: Read nullable values safely and provide defaults only for null or undefined.
rules: Optional chaining stops when its left operand is null or undefined.
Nullish coalescing preserves false, zero, and empty strings.
Use strictNullChecks to distinguish nullable values in the type system.

title: Utility types
summary: Derive common type variations using built-in utility types.
rules: These helpers transform types without changing runtime values.
Partial, Required, and Readonly affect the immediate properties only.
Pick/Omit select properties by key; Record describes a key/value object type.

title: Key queries and indexed access
summary: Derive valid keys and the types of their corresponding values.
rules: keyof produces a union of permitted property keys.
Indexed access in type position selects a property type rather than reading a value.
Numeric and symbol keys are possible; keyof is not always a string union.

title: Mapped and conditional types
summary: Transform property sets or select types using a type-level condition.
rules: Mapped types iterate over a union of property keys.
Mapped modifiers can add or remove readonly and optional markers.
Conditional types with a naked type parameter distribute over unions; tuple wrapping can disable distribution.

title: Assertions, const assertions, and satisfies
summary: Check compatibility or guide static inference without runtime validation.
rules: An assertion changes the checker’s view and does not validate runtime input.
as const preserves literal types and marks literal object properties and tuple elements readonly.
satisfies checks compatibility while preserving useful expression inference; it requires TypeScript 4.9+.

title: Enums
summary: Define a named set of runtime constants.
syntax:
enum Numeric { First, Second, Explicit = 10 }
enum Text { First = "first", Second = "second" }
rules: Ordinary enums generate a runtime object.
Numeric members can auto-increment; string members require initializers.
String literal unions can describe alternatives without generating a runtime enum.
